exposure: Desflurane combined with remifentanil in general anesthesia
Sevoflurane combined with remifentanil in general anesthesia
outcome: Hemodynamics stability (heart rates, mean arterial pressures)
Clinical indexes (operation times, fetal delivery times, intraoperative bleeding volumes, oxytocin volumes, carboprost tromethamine proportions, recovery and extubation times)
pH values of umbilical arterial blood
cohort: The study participants were pregnant women scheduled for cesarean section under general anesthesia.
finding: The desflurane and remifentanil group showed significantly improved mean arterial pressures and heart rates at specific time points, shorter recovery and extubation times, with no significant differences in neonatal outcomes (umbilical arterial blood pH, Apgar scores) or adverse reactions compared to the sevoflurane and remifentanil group.
mod_finding: The study found that desflurane combined with remifentanil improved maternal hemodynamics and shortened recovery times during cesarean section without affecting newborn outcomes compared to sevoflurane.
